plants.title: Cantor's theorem
plants.blurb: There is no way to list all subsets of a set using the set's own elements: for any map `f` from a type `α` to its subsets, some subset is missed. (The subset `{a | a ∉ f a}` cannot be `f a` for any `a`.)

decls.name: ProofGarden.cantor
decls.doc: No function from a type to its powerset (`α → Prop`) is surjective: there is always a subset `s` that `f` never hits.
decls.statement: theorem cantor {α : Type} (f : α → (α → Prop)) : ¬ ∀ s : α → Prop, ∃ a, f a = s

plants.title: Euclid's lemma
plants.blurb: If a prime divides a product, it divides one of the factors. This is the fact that makes prime factorisations unique.

decls.name: ProofGarden.euclids_lemma
decls.doc: If `p` is prime and `p ∣ a * b`, then `p ∣ a` or `p ∣ b`.
decls.statement: theorem euclids_lemma {p a b : Nat} (hp : IsPrime p) (h : p ∣ a * b) : p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b

plants.title: Neighbouring Fibonacci numbers are coprime
plants.blurb: Two consecutive Fibonacci numbers never share a factor bigger than 1. Running Euclid's algorithm on them just walks the sequence back down to `fib 1 = 1`.

plants.title: Gauss's sum
plants.blurb: The numbers from 1 to `n` add up to `n(n+1)/2`, the trick young Gauss is said to have used to add 1 to 100 in seconds.

decls.name: ProofGarden.gauss_sum
decls.statement: theorem gauss_sum (n : Nat) : sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i) = n * (n + 1) / 2

plants.title: Euclid: there are infinitely many primes
plants.blurb: However large a number `n` you pick, there is a prime bigger than it. (Any prime factor of `n! + 1` works: it cannot be ≤ `n`, since those all divide `n!`.)

decls.name: ProofGarden.infinitely_many_primes
decls.doc: For every `n` there is a prime `p` with `n < p`.
decls.statement: theorem infinitely_many_primes (n : Nat) : ∃ p, n < p ∧ IsPrime p

plants.title: Nicomachus's theorem
plants.blurb: The sum of the first cubes is the square of the sum of the first numbers: `1³ + 2³ + ... + n³ = (1 + 2 + ... + n)²`.

decls.name: ProofGarden.nicomachus
decls.statement: theorem nicomachus (n : Nat) : sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i ^ 3) = (sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i)) ^ 2

plants.title: The pigeonhole principle
plants.blurb: Put more pigeons than holes and two pigeons must share a hole.

decls.name: ProofGarden.pigeonhole
decls.doc: If `m < n`, any map from `n` things to `m` things sends two different things to the same place.
decls.statement: theorem pigeonhole {n m : Nat} (h : m < n) (f : Fin n → Fin m) : ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ f i = f j

plants.title: Powers of two add up to one less than the next
plants.blurb: `1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ - 1`: a binary number made of `n` ones is one short of `2ⁿ`. Stated with `+ 1` on the left to avoid natural-number subtraction.

decls.name: ProofGarden.sum_powers_of_two
decls.statement: theorem sum_powers_of_two (n : Nat) : sumRange n (fun i => 2 ^ i) + 1 = 2 ^ n

plants.title: √2 is irrational
plants.blurb: There is no fraction `p / q` whose square is exactly 2. Stated without real numbers: no natural numbers `p` and `q ≠ 0` satisfy `p² = 2q²`.

decls.name: ProofGarden.sqrt_two_irrational
decls.doc: There are no natural numbers `p, q` with `q ≠ 0` and `p * p = 2 * q * q`.
decls.statement: theorem sqrt_two_irrational : ¬ ∃ p q : Nat, q ≠ 0 ∧ p * p = 2 * q * q

plants.title: The first n odd numbers add up to n²
plants.blurb: `1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n - 1) = n²`. Picture each odd number as an L-shaped layer wrapped around a square.

decls.name: ProofGarden.sum_of_odds
decls.statement: theorem sum_of_odds (n : Nat) : sumRange n (fun i => 2 * i + 1) = n * n

plants.title: Lemma: facts about the factorial
plants.blurb: Two small facts Euclid's proof needs: `n!` is never zero, and every number from 1 to `n` divides `n!`.

decls.name: ProofGarden.fact_pos
decls.doc: The factorial of any number is positive.

decls.name: ProofGarden.dvd_fact
decls.statement: theorem dvd_fact {k n : Nat} (h₁ : 1 ≤ k) (h₂ : k ≤ n) : k ∣ fact n

plants.title: Lemma: twice the sum 0 + 1 + ... + n is n(n+1)
plants.blurb: Gauss's pairing trick without division: writing the sum forwards and backwards and adding gives `n` pairs of `n + 1`. Stated without `/` so it can be proved by plain induction.

decls.name: ProofGarden.two_mul_sum_upto
decls.statement: theorem two_mul_sum_upto (n : Nat) : 2 * sumRange (n + 1) (fun i => i) = n * (n + 1)

plants.title: Lemma: if a square is even, the number is even
plants.blurb: An odd number times an odd number is odd, so if `p * p` is even then `p` is.

decls.name: ProofGarden.two_dvd_of_two_dvd_mul_self
decls.statement: theorem two_dvd_of_two_dvd_mul_self {p : Nat} (h : 2 ∣ p * p) : 2 ∣ p

plants.title: Lemma: every number ≥ 2 has a prime factor
plants.blurb: The smallest divisor of `n` that is at least 2 is prime.

decls.name: ProofGarden.exists_prime_factor
decls.doc: Every natural number `n ≥ 2` is divisible by some prime.
decls.statement: theorem exists_prime_factor {n : Nat} (h : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ p, IsPrime p ∧ p ∣ n
